name: Kaylene Stocking
title: Research Assistant Professor
department: Computer Science; affiliated Robot Intelligence through Perception Lab
fitReason: Mechanistic VLA interpretability research identifies semantic activation directions that can change physical policy behavior. A September 2026 TTIC grant adds curiosity-driven robot learning with progressively expanding physical abilities; that grant is a research direction rather than completed hardware evidence.

physicalEvidence.summary: The August/September 2025 Berkeley work physically executes Low/High height-steered pi0-FAST policies on a UR5 with Robotiq 2F-140 gripper. For the Slow/Fast comparison, alternative steering actions are inferred in parallel but only the unmodified baseline actions are executed. Thus speed steering is counterfactual analysis, not executed physical speed interventions. Current TTIC hardware access is unconfirmed.

shortVisit.summary: RIPL explicitly invites Visiting Student Program applications and lists Stocking as affiliated research faculty. TTIC confirms RAP faculty may host interns, and the formal program accepts graduate/international applicants whose applications go to named faculty. Stocking’s personal 2027 intake is not confirmed.

scoreReasons.fit: Direct mechanistic foundation-policy interpretability and embodied-learning fit.
scoreReasons.physical: Height-steered UR5 rollouts were physically executed in earlier Berkeley work; speed comparison was counterfactual on baseline-executed trajectories, not current TTIC hardware.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: Conservative credit for lab/program route and documented RAP hosting authority; personal intake and eight-week exception unknown.
scoreReasons.freshness: 2025 primary hardware paper plus September 2026 official research activity.

Apply roughly five to six months ahead; English proficiency is required before an offer, plus insurance and student-life privileges. Funding varies and volunteer visits sometimes occur. Physical evidence predates the TTIC appointment and does not establish local UR5 access. No current TTIC personal email was found; the paper’s Berkeley correspondence address is historical. Use the verified program contact for routing rather than guessing.

name: Jeff Schneider
title: Research Professor
department: Robotics Institute, School of Computer Science
fitReason: Latent Policy Steering (September 2026) pretrains an optical-flow world model on heterogeneous embodiments, then uses it to steer Diffusion Policy or pi0.5 on a target robot with limited demonstrations.

physicalEvidence.summary: The primary paper explicitly evaluates a physical Franka with wrist and fixed cameras on radish placement, salad sweeping, bead scooping and towel folding. These trials are separate from its Robomimic simulation results.

shortVisit.summary: The current faculty page advertises postdocs and centralized PhD admissions. Its current CMU master’s students are mentoring precedent only; no external short-term master’s pathway is stated.

scoreReasons.fit: Direct cross-embodiment world-model and VLA manipulation fit.
scoreReasons.physical: Four named manipulation tasks executed on physical Franka.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: No explicit external summer-master’s recruitment route.
scoreReasons.freshness: September 2026 primary experiment and current official faculty record.
